newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military college wraps up disciplinary hearings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military college wraps up disciplinary hearings.

text.p: The Citadel military college wrapped up closed disciplinary hearings Sunday for 11 cadets accused of participating in hazing of some of the school's first women cadets, Citadel spokesman Terry Leedom said.
The outcome of deliberations by two commandant boards and a hearing officer was expected Wednesday, but Leedom said that is now doubtful.
Three cadets, two seniors and a junior, were charged with physical violence, abusive treatment, failure to report hazing and poor judgment. They could be expelled if found guilty.
The eight other cadets faced lesser charges, including failure to report hazing and sexual harassment.
Jeanie Mentavlos and Kim Messer, the women the men were accused of hazing, did not attend the hearings.
Their attorneys, Tim Kulp and Paul Gibson, said in a letter to the school that they did not want the women there because their lawyers could not participate or record the hearings independently.

"Our clients remain ready, willing, and able to offer sworn testimony in any judicial proceedings wherein witnesses are placed under oath, rights to counsel are fully recognised ... proceedings are open to the public and a reliable record of these proceedings is made," the letter said.
Messer and Mentavlos withdrew from the Citadel in January. They were among four women enrolled at the state-funded school after it changed its all-male admissions policy last summer.
Among other things, they claimed the clothing they were wearning was sprayed with fingernail polish remover and then set on fire.
